title: Leaky token reservoir with grace-token windows and regional stall safeguard
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a leaky-token reservoir admission layer that provides short, bounded grace tokens for tenants during transient limiter outages or regional latency spikes. The reservoir is a small credit pool per tenant that refills slowly (leaky bucket style) but can dispense a fixed number of emergency tokens (grace window) to absorb short bursts without violating SLOs. A lightweight regional safeguard replicates reservoir metadata to a peer region to enable proportional failover when a regional limiter becomes unavailable.
problem_statement: Current limiter outages and transient control-plane stalls cause either large-scale hard rejects (customer-visible 429s) or aggressive degradation that harms high-priority tenants. We lack a mechanism to absorb short bursts and to continue serving critical traffic during limiter failover without violating multi-tenant fairness or SLO budgets.
goals: Provide a bounded grace window (short burst absorption) per tenant to reduce customer-visible 429s during transient limiter delays
Ensure fairness: grace dispensing respects tenant weights and SLO budgets
Enable multi-region proportional failover with a read-mostly metadata replication that does not require synchronous quorum
Integrate with circuit-breakers so degraded-mode shedding can opt into reservoir-backed short-term serving
Deliver observability: per-tenant grace consumption, refill rates, and cross-region divergence metrics
non_goals: Replace existing quota accounting for long-running heavy traffic patterns
Provide unlimited burst capacity—grace tokens are intentionally bounded
Complex cross-region consensus; design favors eventual consistency and safety
design_notes: Reservoir model: each tenant has two counters: stable_credits (normal quota) and grace_credits (emergency pool). grace_credits caps at a small integer (default 10) and refills at a slow rate (e.g. 1 token / 30s).

Admission flow: request checks stable_credits -> allow. If stable_credits exhausted, attempt deduct from grace_credits if tenant weight and global emergency budget permit. If both fail, follow existing 429 path or degraded fallback.

Regional safeguard: replicate (tenant_id, grace_credits, last_refill_ts, weight) to a single peer region asynchronously. On local limiter control-plane loss, the region can consult last-known peer values and apply a proportional cap (e.g. 50% of combined grace) to avoid double-spend.

Circuit-breaker integration: when a circuit trips, the limiter toggles a degraded flag and switches from strict quota to reservoir-first mode for a configurable period, allowing critical tenants to consume limited grace while lower-priority tenants get a stricter backoff.
Fairness: grace consumption enforces tenant weights by converting token cost into weighted units (cost = 1 / weight), and a per-window smoothing ensures high-frequency borrowers do not starve others.
Safety: implement TTL-based tombstones for tenant metadata to avoid stale cross-region replication causing accidental over-granting.
implementation_steps: 1) Add reservoir data structure to limiter hot path (in-memory + persistent checkpoint in Redis/etcd).
2) Implement grace credit refill loop and per-tenant caps with config knobs per tier (free/dev/enterprise).
3) Add admission logic branch and unit tests for edge cases (concurrent consumption, wraparound, double-consume prevention).
4) Implement async replication sender and receiver with compressor + tombstone semantics for region peer.
5) Integrate with existing circuit-breaker flags and degraded-mode admission flow.
6) Add metrics: grace_consumed, grace_refilled, forbidden_by_grace, cross_region_divergence, reservoir_checkpoint_latency.
7) End-to-end chaos test simulating limiter outage + region failover (see test plan).
8) Docs + runbook + postmortem template for incidents involving reservoir.
acceptance_criteria: System correctly dispenses grace_credits under normal load for all tenant tiers and respects per-tenant caps
Under simulated control-plane stall, the regional safeguard allows proportional continued serving without double-spend in >99.9% of exercised scenarios
Telemetry surfaces per-tenant grace usage and an alert fires when cross-region divergence exceeds configured threshold (default 2 tokens)
No measurable increase in 95th latency for admitted requests (target: <5ms added overhead) in steady-state benchmarks
Unit+integration tests cover concurrent decrements and replication race windows
Runbook tested with one simulated incident, including rollback path to disable reservoir feature at runtime
test_plan: Unit tests for refill math, cap enforcement, and weight-adjusted costing
Integration tests: two-region simulator with replicated metadata and failover scenario
Load test: 1000 tenants with mix of weights, measure 429 reduction during transient limiter delay injection
Chaos test: kill limiter control process in region A while ramping traffic; verify region B's safeguard keeps critical tenants served proportionally
Performance microbench: measure per-request CPU and latency overhead on hot path
Regression: ensure existing quota consistency invariants remain satisfied after checkpointing
rollback_plan: Runtime feature flag to disable reservoir; disable replication and allow all regions to revert to strict quota. Operations runbook includes steps to set global feature flag, purge reservoir state, and rehydrate stable quotas from last committed checkpoint.
telemetry_and_alerts: Alert: GRACE_DIVERGENCE_HIGH fires when cross_region_divergence_count > 50 in 5m
SLO: reduce transient-429s by 60% for targeted tenants in simulated outages
